title: The browser (wasm32) build of CamCraft loads from the GitHub Pages site

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Asked for by the maintainer, 2026-11-12: "the wasm32 app should be loadable from the github pages for easy access". Filed by an agent for him (no `source:agent`: it is his request).

**Where things stand**
- GitHub Pages is now enabled for this repo (source: GitHub Actions) at https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/. The `site` and `pages` jobs of `release.yml` build the Zola site in `site/` and deploy it on a release tag (#688). The `github-pages` environment allows `v*.*.0` tags to deploy.
- The wasm32 shell runs in a browser on WebGL2 (#31, PR #847): `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` writes `<target>/web/` with `index.html`, `wasi_shim.js`, `camcraft-ui.js` and `camcraft-ui_bg.wasm`. Nothing publishes that folder; today it only runs from a local http server.
- The site's front page already says the browser build comes "once the app and its interface build for the web".

**What is wanted**
The released wasm32 build is served from the Pages site, so anyone can open CamCraft in a browser from a link, without installing anything.
- The app lives under a fixed path of the site (e.g. `/Camcraft/app/`), with a clear link from the front page and the guide's first-run page.
- It is built in the release workflow from the tagged tree (a job that runs `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` and hands its output to the `site` job, which places it in the Pages artifact) - **no new `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger** (Actions budget). Linux runner; say in the PR how many billed minutes it adds to a cut.
- Everything the page loads resolves under the project sub-path (`/Camcraft/app/...`, not `/`): the import map, `wasi_shim.js`, the `.js`/`.wasm` pair, any asset fetch. A fork's own Pages (another owner or repo name) must work too, as the `site` job's `--base-url` already does.
- The page says what it is: the version it was built from, that it runs in the browser on WebGL2, and what does not work there yet (the list on #31: file picker, playback without threads, WebGPU).
- A failed wasm build must not withhold the docs site or the release: the docs deploy without `/app/` and the run names what failed (the way `publish` treats a failed platform build).

**Known obstacles**
- #949: the build script rewrites the checkout's `Cargo.lock`; in CI that must not leak into anything packaged from the same checkout.
- `.wasm` size and Pages limits (1 GB site, 100 MB per file): state the size in the PR; use `wasm-opt` if it is needed and available without a new unpinned download.
- Pages serves no custom headers (no COOP/COEP), so nothing may depend on `SharedArrayBuffer` / threads.

Done means: after a release tag, `https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/app/` loads the shell of that release in a current Chrome and Firefox, linked from the site's front page; pinned by a check in the workflow that the Pages artifact holds `app/index.html` and the `.wasm`, and by a test or script check that the page's URLs are relative to its own folder.

Part of #688 (docs and browser build on Pages); builds on #31 (the app and UI on wasm).
